performance.cl_max_land_source: Airbus A320 Aircraft Characteristics Rev 46, 1 Jul 2026, section 3-5-0 p.1: threshold IAS 136 kt at MLW 66,000 kg, maximum certified flap, standard atmosphere; https://mediaassets.airbus.com/pm_38_916_916266-iujedqawwy.pdf?fileName=aca32001-jul-2026-2.pdf; existing 122.6 m^2 gross-area input supported by secondary Flugzeuginfo A320 technical data, https://www.flugzeuginfo.net/acdata_php/acdata_a320_en.php; CLmax_land recovered as 2*m*g/(rho*S*(Vref/1.23)^2), rho=1.225 kg/m^3; WV017 mass matches; planning IAS treated as sea-level CAS, rounded whole-knot speed; Airbus marks the speed for information only
performance.cl_max_to_source: Raymer, Aircraft Design: A Conceptual Approach, 5th ed., Eq. 12.21 and Table 12.2 (printed p. 415): CLmax_TO = clean 1.500 + 0.7 x flap 0.849 + leading edge 0.286 (landing flap increment 0.9 dcl_max Sflapped/Sref cos(hinge sweep); c'/c 1.275 flap, 1.075 slat; declared control-surface spans); Jane's All the World's Aircraft 2008-09, Airbus A320 entry, PDF p. 315: five-segment leading-edge slats per wing, two-segment Fowler trailing-edge flaps, slats 18/22/27 deg and flaps 10/15/20/35 deg; PDF p. 316 flap area 21.10 m2 (cross-check: 21.10/0.30 chord = 0.58 Sref flapped). Conceptual handbook estimate, not a measured CLmax: the 60-80 % take-off share is taken at its 70 % midpoint, flap and slat span and chord are the declared control-surface defaults, and the clean coefficient is the configuration's 1.5 class value.

performance.cl_max_land_source: ATR 72-600 PW127M/N Factsheet, 2020, p.2: reference speed at landing 113 KIAS, basic MLW 22,350 kg, reference wing area 61 m^2; https://www.atr-aircraft.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/07/Factsheets_-_ATR_72-600.pdf; CLmax_land recovered as 2*m*g/(rho*S*(Vref/1.23)^2), rho=1.225 kg/m^3; Reference speed grouped with the basic-MLW sea-level landing performance; source does not explicitly repeat its speed mass or IAS correction, so basic MLW and IAS=CAS are declared conceptual assumptions
performance.cl_max_to_source: ATR 72-600 PW127M/N Factsheet, 2020, p.2: Take-off speed (V2 min @ MTOW) 116 KCAS; weight table includes option-1 MTOW 23,000 kg and wing area 61 m^2; https://www.atr-aircraft.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/07/Factsheets_-_ATR_72-600.pdf; effective model CLmax_TO recovered as 2*m*g/(rho*S*(V2_min/1.2430)^2), rho=1.225 kg/m^3; The single family-wide V2 minimum line is not column-paired with the 22,800 kg basic or 23,000 kg optional MTOW; assigning it to the preset's 23,000 kg option is a declared applicability assumption. The minimum is taken as the model-selected V2; the model V2/VSR is the CS 25.107 rule max(selected 1.20, V2MIN 1.13 VSR, 1.10 VMC estimate = 1.10 x 1.13 VSR) = 1.243, so the published minimum is inverted with that ratio. Flap configuration and whether V2 min is stall-, control- or climb-limited are unpublished. Effective lift recovery does not establish measured CLmax, VMC or a certified V2 schedule; speed reconstruction is an input check, not independent validation. Source CAS is interpreted on the ISA sea-level equivalent-density basis.

performance.cl_max_land_source: Boeing Airport Compatibility Engineering, FAA Reference Code and Approach Speeds for Boeing Aircraft, 30 Mar 2016, p.3: 787-9 approach speed 153 kt, MLW 425,000 lb; https://www.boeing.com/content/dam/boeing/v2/airports/faq/arcandapproachspeeds.pdf; 360.464 m^2 (3,880 ft^2) is the preset's own planform area, used for both this recovery and the model so Vref is reproduced (Boeing prints no wing area; an untraceable 377 m^2 OpenAP/secondary value, 4.4 % larger, was used before 2026-10-07 and made the model Vref 156.5 kt against 153 kt published); CLmax_land recovered as 2*m*g/(rho*S*(Vref/1.23)^2), rho=1.225 kg/m^3; Legacy 561,500 lb MTW / 425,000 lb MLW source matches the preset mass; area origin unverified (flugzeuginfo.net 361.0 m^2 corroborates); manufacturer planning speed treated as sea-level CAS; effective gross-area coefficient is distinct from the generic takeoff CLmax assumption
performance.cl_max_to_source: Raymer, Aircraft Design: A Conceptual Approach, 5th ed., Eq. 12.21 and Table 12.2 (printed p. 415): CLmax_TO = clean 1.500 + 0.7 x flap 0.859 + leading edge 0.242 (landing flap increment 0.9 dcl_max Sflapped/Sref cos(hinge sweep); c'/c 1.275 flap, 1.075 slat; declared control-surface spans); EASA TCDS IM.A.115 (library easa_2025_b787tcds) lists Krueger flaps (D-05-9); Jane's All the World's Aircraft 2008-09, Boeing 787 entry, PDF p. 742: inboard and outboard flaps with spoilers ahead of each, variable-camber trailing edge. Flap slot count and the Krueger span share (one inboard Krueger in four leading-edge sections) are assumptions. Conceptual handbook estimate, not a measured CLmax: the 60-80 % take-off share is taken at its 70 % midpoint, flap and slat span and chord are the declared control-surface defaults, and the clean coefficient is the configuration's 1.5 class value.
